notes: ncert.nic.in (textbook.php and the textbook PDF/prelims files) refused automated fetching (robots.txt disallow) on 2026-10-19, so the NCERT contents pages, printed section headings and edition/reprint lines could not be read directly. Chapter titles were verified instead against other official government sources: NCERT's CIET audio-book pages (ciet.ncert.gov.in) and the Delhi Directorate of Education 2026-27 syllabus (edustud.nic.in), which prescribes NCERT books. 'verified': true means the title was seen in at least one of those sources.

CBSE does not publish its own mathematics syllabus for Grades 6-8. Its 2026-27 curriculum release (Circular Acad-14/2026) covers Classes IX-XII only, and CBSE circulars direct schools to the new NCERT textbooks. The 2026-27 prescription is therefore inferred from those circulars plus the Delhi DoE 2026-27 syllabus. No CBSE or NCERT notice found replaces or withdraws Ganita Prakash for 2026-27.

Section titles come from the subtopic lists in the Delhi DoE 2026-27 annual syllabus, not from the printed textbook. They appear to quote the textbook's section headings, but DoE may have shortened, merged or left some out (its list is 'for assessment purpose only'), and capitalisation follows DoE. Check them against the printed NCERT book before using them as exact headings.

Learning outcomes are written by the compiler from the chapter and section scope. They are not copied from NCERT's Learning Outcomes document, which was not consulted because ncert.nic.in was inaccessible.

Secondary sites (teachoo.com, edzy.ai, esaral.com, aglasem.com, collegedunia.com) were used only to locate official documents and to cross-check chapter order and titles. Nothing was taken from them as authoritative.

Grade 8: the new NCERT book (Ganita Prakash) came in from 2025-26 (CBSE Circulars Acad-12/2025 and Acad-48/2025). The Delhi DoE 2026-27 Grade 8 syllabus prescribes 'NCERT Class VIII Mathematics Part I' for Term I and 'Part II' for Term II, with the chapter lists used here, so both parts are in use in 2026-27.

Chapter numbering starts again at 1 in Part II. Here 'term' records the book part (1 = Part I, 2 = Part II), and chapter ids follow the term-book pattern (cbse-g08-t1-c01 ... cbse-g08-t2-c07). In the Delhi DoE plan Part I = Term I and Part II = Term II. CBSE itself does not set terms for Grade 8.

Part II chapter titles were verified only against the Delhi DoE 2026-27 syllabus. No NCERT page for Part II (CIET audio book, contents page or library record) could be found or opened. Secondary sites agree on the same seven titles in the same order.

Part II Ch 2: the source prints 'THE BAUDHAYANAPYTHAGORAS THEOREM' (hyphen lost), while the subtopic list writes 'Baudhāyana - Pythagoras'. The title 'The Baudhāyana-Pythagoras Theorem' is a best reconstruction. The diacritic and dash style of the printed title were not verified.
Part I Ch 6 title: DoE prints 'WE DISTRIBUTE, YET THINGS MULTIPLY' (with comma). The CIET file name has no punctuation.

Part I Ch 6 sections: DoE lists 'Mind the Mistake' / 'Mend the Mistake' and 'This Way or That Way' / 'All Ways Lead to the Bay' as separate items. These are probably single headings in the book ('Mind the Mistake, Mend the Mistake' and 'This Way or That Way, All Ways Lead to the Bay'). They are kept as DoE wrote them.

Part I Ch 1 and Ch 5: DoE's subtopic lists are shorter than secondary topic lists (e.g. 'Square and cube roots', 'Sum of consecutive numbers' are not listed by DoE). The outcomes cover the wider scope seen in secondary sources, and the section lists stay as DoE gave them. Items such as 'Spreadsheets' (Ch 5 and Part II Ch 5) and 'Supercells' (Part II Ch 3) may be boxed activities rather than numbered sections.
Part II edition: the release date of Part II (expected during 2025-26) and its edition statement were not verified.

Part II Ch 1 (Fractions in Disguise): it was not verified whether the chapter includes percentage increase/decrease, discounts, profit and loss, or interest. No outcomes were written for those topics. Check the printed chapter and add them if present (MATH.number.profit-loss would then apply).

outcomes.statement: Recognise perfect squares and use their properties (possible last digits, sums of consecutive odd numbers, numbers between consecutive squares).

proposed.name: Relate figurate number sequences to their dot and shape pictures
proposed.why: Existing pattern competencies cover extending patterns and stating rules; none covers square/triangular/cube number sequences, their pictorial representations and the relations between them (e.g. sums of odd numbers are squares).

outcomes.statement: Find square roots of perfect squares (e.g. by prime factorisation or by repeatedly subtracting odd numbers) and estimate square roots of other numbers between consecutive integers.

proposed.name: Express a number as a product of primes
proposed.why: The only existing mention is inside MATH.number.euclid-algorithm (Grade 10, combined with the Euclidean algorithm); Grade 6 needs prime factorisation as a standalone skill.

outcomes.statement: Find cubes and cube roots of perfect cubes and recognise perfect cubes.
Explore and explain patterns involving squares and cubes, such as cubes as sums of consecutive odd numbers or numbers that are sums of two cubes in two ways.

proposed.name: Formulate and test conjectures from number explorations
proposed.why: MATH.reasoning.counterexamples-intro (Grade 5) is about testing a given generalisation; Ganita Prakash repeatedly asks learners to generate conjectures from explorations (Kaprekar, Collatz, palindromes, consecutive sums) and test them systematically.
